{"description":"## What

The workspace declares rust-version = "1.88" (raised from 1.87 on 2026-11-24, and from 1.73 before that). Nothing checks it.

The only CI workflow is .github/workflows/diff-harness.yml, and its line 28 comment reads: 'Stable Rust toolchain only. MSRV 1.73 enforcement is a separate concern'. That comment is itself two MSRV bumps stale, which is evidence of the problem rather than merely an example of it.

## Why this bites

A developer on a current toolchain cannot notice an MSRV violation locally. The machine this was found on runs rustc 1.100.0, so every crate in the workspace builds regardless of what rust-version claims. An MSRV regression is therefore invisible until a downstream consumer on the declared minimum tries to build — at which point the workspace has been lying in its published metadata, possibly for several releases.

This was found while adding hickory-resolver to pkix-dane-resolver: every 0.26.x release requires 1.88 while the workspace declared 1.87. Catching it took reading "cargo info" output by hand, one version at a time. Nothing would have caught it otherwise.

## Fix

Add a CI job that builds the workspace with the declared MSRV toolchain. Two usual shapes:

- A dedicated job pinning the toolchain to the declared version (dtolnay/rust-toolchain with an explicit version, or equivalent) running "cargo check --workspace --all-features". Simple, but the pinned version must be updated in lockstep with the declaration, which is the same class of drift as the stale comment.
- cargo-msrv, or "cargo hack --version-range", which read rust-version from the manifest rather than duplicating it. Preferred: nothing to keep in sync.

Either way, also fix the stale comment at diff-harness.yml line 28.

## Worth considering alongside

The repository has exactly one workflow, and it is the differential-test harness. The quality gates this workspace actually runs — fmt, clippy with --all-targets --all-features, rustdoc with -D warnings, typos, and cargo hack --depth 2 — appear to be run by hand. If so, MSRV is one instance of a broader gap, and that is the more useful thing to fix. Confirm before scoping.

## Acceptance

[ ] CI fails when any crate requires a newer toolchain than the declared MSRV
[ ] The MSRV is read from the manifest rather than duplicated in CI config, or the duplication is documented as needing lockstep updates
[ ] diff-harness.yml line 28's stale '1.73' comment corrected"}

CLOSED 2026-11-24. The bead's scope question answered yes, so the fix is a full quality-gates workflow rather than an MSRV-only one -- and running the MSRV check for the first time found a live violation.

## The violation this bead was filed to prevent was already present

cargo check --workspace --all-features on the declared MSRV FAILED: uuid 1.29, reached via moka <- hickory-resolver <- pkix-dane-resolver, requires rustc 1.89 while the workspace declared 1.88. A consumer on the declared minimum could not build pkix-chain with dane-resolver enabled. Introduced when hickory was added for PKIX-j32w.2; invisible locally because current stable compiles it fine.

Root cause: resolver = "2" ignores rust-version when resolving. Fixed by moving to resolver = "3", which is MSRV-aware -- re-resolving picked uuid 1.26 on its own and annotated the newer release as requiring 1.89. Chosen over a lockfile pin because the lockfile is not what a consumer resolves against: pinning would have fixed this repository and left every downstream consumer on 1.88 with the same broken tree.

Verified by installing 1.88 into a throwaway RUSTUP_HOME under the session scratchpad, since /usr/local/rustup is not writable here.

## Scope: the broader gap was real

The bead asked to confirm before scoping. Confirmed: the only workflow was diff-harness.yml. No CI for fmt, clippy, rustdoc, typos, tests, feature combinations or MSRV. So quality-gates.yml covers all of them.

Every command was run locally before being written into the workflow. The feature matrix covers 199 combinations; all gates pass.

## A CI design problem found by running it

Workspace clippy with -D warnings failed on PRE-EXISTING findings: clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks in pkix-path and pkix-difftest. Several crates opt into clippy::pedantic, and that is a NEW pedantic lint.

So a lint job on floating stable would turn CI red every few Rust releases for reasons unrelated to any change, which is how a gate gets switched off. The lint job therefore PINS its toolchain, bumped deliberately; the test, MSRV and feature jobs do not, since they compile rather than lint and a new compiler breaking them is a signal worth having promptly.

The three findings were fixed rather than shipping red CI. One in pkix-path was declined and documented with #[expect] and a reason: the iterator is stored in DirStringBytes::Bmp, so converting it rewrites that variant's field type and the Iterator impl transcoding UCS-2 -- a real edit to DN-comparison code for a style preference.

Incidentally found: pkix-chain listed pkix-dane-resolver as an optional dependency no code referenced, so enabling dane-resolver pulled the DNS stack without giving the consumer access to it. Now re-exported as dane_resolver.

## Acceptance

[x] CI fails when any crate requires a newer toolchain than the declared MSRV
[x] The MSRV is read from the manifest rather than duplicated in CI config
[x] diff-harness.yml's stale '1.73' comment corrected, and pointed at the sibling workflow that now does the enforcing

## Left open deliberately

The typos step names the five crates that are clean rather than running over the repository, which is not typos-clean as a whole (43 findings when last counted). That is noted in the workflow itself: a gate permitted to fail is not a gate, so the rest wants cleaning before the path list comes out. Filed separately.

Also unverified: the workflow has never run on GitHub. The commands are verified locally and the YAML parses, but Actions-specific behaviour -- the toolchain actions, the cache action, taiki-e/install-action -- will only be exercised on the first push.
